questions.question:
If M denotes '-', N denotes '÷', O denotes '×' and P denotes '+', then what will come in place of '?' in the following equation?

(14 O 7) P 41 M (26 O 3) P (176 N 2) = ?
questions.solution:
BODMAS rule is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/13bc0065c96e715682af7c8a6dc1b4c567b7a2a89597cc68809a5ff942c7e421.png] 

We have the equation given as (14 O 7) P 41 M (26 O 3) P (176 N 2) = ?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6d6cc5062d1b7ba205fef899de45e1bd6f9423498f5626d9265538ab560392cc.png] 

Using this above, decode it, we will get, 

= (14 × 7) + 41 - (26 × 3) + (176 ÷ 2) 

Applying BODMAS rule, we will get,

= __**(14 **____**×**____** 7) **__+ 41 -__** (26 **____**×**____** 3) **__+ 88

= __**98 + 41**__ - 78 __**+ 88**__

= 149

Hence, the answer is '__**149**__' for the given equation. .

questions.question: The second number in the given number pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number pairs, except one. Find that odd number pair.
questions.solution:
The logic here is:

**Logic: (First number)² + 5 = Second number.**

So, we will check the options one by one: 

1) 6 : 41 ⇒ (6)² + 5 = 36 + 5 = 41

2) 4 : 21 ⇒ (4)² + 5 = 16 + 5 = 21

3) 8 : 70 ⇒ (8)² + 5 = **69 ≠ 70**

4) 7 : 54 ⇒ (7)² + 5 = 49 + 5 = 54

Hence, the number pair '__**8 : 70**__' is the odd one out.

questions.question:
Which two numbers, from amongst the given options, should be interchanged to make the given equation correct?

(132 ÷ 12) + (6 × 11) + 18 - (64 ÷ 16) × 8 = 70
questions.solution:
BODMAS Rule is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/97072bdd1f5e802223d1f8f5b1a4b12c68165fa67f70d7e53e21992716e4924c.png] 

Given : (132 ÷ 12) + (6 × 11) + 18 - (64 ÷ 16) × 8 = 70

First, we will check all the options as below:

1) 11 and 8

Rightarrow __**(132 ÷ 12)**__ + __**(6 × 8) **__+ 18 - __(64 ÷ 16)__ × 11 = 70

Applying BODMAS rule we will get,

Rightarrow 11 +__** **____**(6 × 8) **__+ 18 - 4 × 11 = 70

Rightarrow __**11 + 48 + 18**__ - 44 = 70

Rightarrow 33 ≠ 70, this is not possible

2) 12 and 6

Rightarrow __**(132 ÷ 6)**__ + __**(12 × 11)**__ + 18 - __**(64 ÷ 16)**__ × 8 = 70

Applying BODMAS rule we will get,

Rightarrow 22 + **__(12 × 11__**) + 18 - 4 × 8 = 70

Rightarrow __**12 + 132 + 18 **__- 32 = 70

Rightarrow 130 ≠ 70, this is not possible

3) 8 and 6

Rightarrow __**(132 ÷ 12) **__+ (**__6 × 11)__** + 18 - __**(64 ÷ 16)**__ × 8 = 70

Applying BODMAS rule we will get,

Rightarrow 11 + __**(6 × 11)**__ + 18 - 4 × 8 = 70 

Rightarrow __**11 + 66 + 18 **__- 32 = 70

Rightarrow 63 ≠ 70, this is not possible

4) 12 and 11

Rightarrow __**(132 ÷ 11)**__ + (**__6 × 12)__** + 18 - __**(64 ÷ 16)**__ × 8 = 70

Applying BODMAS rule we will get,

Rightarrow 12 + __**(6 × 12**____**)**__ + 18 - 4 × 8 = 70

Rightarrow __**12 + 72 + 18**__ - 32 = 70

Rightarrow 70 = 70, this is possible

Hence, the two numbers '__**12 and 11**__' are interchanged to get the correct equation.

questions.question: If 13 January 2006 is a Friday, then what will be the day of the week on 28 March 2008?
questions.solution:
Here, we have given that:

13 Jan 2006 is Friday.

Since 2007 is an ordinary year = 1 odd day and 2008 is a leap year = 2 odd days

So, 13 Jan 2008 is Friday + 1 + 1 = Sunday (As February is not count)

Next, we will count the remaining days of the month of the year 2008 as:

= 18 (Jan) + 29 (Feb) + 28 (Mar) = 75 = 75/7= 10 weeks and 5 are remaining.

Thus, 28 March 2008 = Sunday + 5 = Friday

Hence, the day will be __**Friday **__28 March 2008.
